sourceBindings.text: A carefully collected sample loses much of its value if nobody can establish where it came from or how it was handled. Protect its identity and follow the preservation method for the actual analysis.
Make a durable, readable container label with all required identity fields and match it to the record.
Choose the container, preservation and transfer timing from the stated laboratory instructions rather than a universal rule.
Record sample handovers and prevent identity mix-ups and cross-contamination.

The link between container and sample identity is uncertain.
Stop guessing; inspect the contemporaneous record and report the discrepancy.
In future, label the container body and check it at each handover.
A lid alone is not a dependable sample identifier.

sourceBindings.text: Card A specifies air drying for a routine fertility submission. Card B specifies fresh cooled soil in an approved sealed container.
Keep A and B separately identified.
Follow each card's preparation, quantity and timing.
Do not seal A indefinitely because B needs moisture retained, or dry B because A needs drying.
The analysis method determines preservation.

sourceBindings.text: A sample required to remain cooled is found in a hot vehicle after several hours.
Record the known interval, condition and any measured temperature without inventing missing readings.
Report the deviation for a method-specific acceptance or resampling decision.
Do not erase the history by recording only the final cooled temperature.
A truthful deviation record is better than an invented uninterrupted cold chain.

sourceBindings.text: Two lids were swapped, two laboratory method cards require different sample conditions, and one cooled sample spent hours in a hot vehicle. Decide what can be trusted, recorded or corrected before transfer.
Build a readable body label and match its unique ID to the field record.
Select dry or fresh-cooled handling from each stated laboratory card, without applying one universal preservation rule.
Document each handover and the known deviation; mark the missing temperature or interval as unknown if it was not recorded.
Flag an identity mismatch for investigation rather than guessing from soil colour.
Creating and checking the real label, container, timing and transfer record remains trainer-observed.

sourceBindings.text: Collect, label and document the training sample
Riverside Park Expansion
Site 3 – Proposed Playground
Use actual collection date/time for real practice; mark a simulated date/time as scenario data.

Demonstration card specifies an approved sealed bag and cooler with ice packs. Actual analyte, container and timing require the receiving laboratory's instructions; no collection from a potentially contaminated playground is authorized.
Select the specified stainless steel trowel, approved sample bag, permanent marker, cooler and Field Data Sheet, plus task protection and a means to check quantity/conditions as required.
Clean the trowel before collecting and prevent cross-contamination.
Collect approximately 500 g from the specified 0–15 cm layer at the authorized safe training point, recording actual quantity/depth rather than equating a cup to 500 g.
Place the material in the approved bag and seal it as required by this cooled-sample scenario.
Label the container body with all six information groups and retained field/group/zone information.
Complete the matched Field Data Sheet; retain individual observation evidence from S1-11.
Record objective colour, texture/feel, moisture and site observations; this shared item is assessed in S1-11.
Place the labeled sealed sample in the cooler as this scenario requires, and record the prescribed preservation check.
Make a transfer entry with sample ID, giver, receiver, date/time and condition.
Check identity and condition with the receiving person and record any discrepancy.

The eight-item collection card continues into S1-11: each learner's real label, transfer and field observations require trainer evidence. Use only authorized safe training material and the receiving laboratory's actual instructions.
